full_judgment: 35. The cardinal principle which has always to be kept in view in our system of administration of justice for criminal cases is that a person arraigned as an accused is presumed to be innocent unless that presumption is rebutted by prosecution. Prosecution has to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt. Proof beyond reasonable doubt means proof of an offence with the certainty of criminal law, the certainty is that the offence has been committed and no other person but the accused person on the evidences on record committed the offence. It is emphasised that the fundamental principle of criminal law is that the boon of doubt arising out of any material point must be showered upon the accused person.
